docs.title: MSF React Modules
docs.text: This repository is the shared React module library for the MSF ecosystem. It packages reusable frontend building blocks and keeps them organized as a workspace so they can be improved and published independently.

docs.title: Repository purpose
docs.text:
The workspace is intended to provide:

  • reusable React modules and shared utilities
  • structured package publishing via pnpm workspaces
  • a consistent release flow through changesets
  • a clean source of frontend primitives for application teams

docs.title: Repository shape
docs.text:
react-modules/
├── configs/
├── packages/
├── scripts/
├── package.json
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml
├── pnpm-lock.yaml
├── README.md
├── mkdocs.yml
├── .github/
└── openwiki/

docs.title: Typical commands
docs.text:
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm lint
pnpm test

docs.title: Operational guidance
docs.text:
• keep package interfaces clear and stable
  • prefer reusable primitives over app-specific code
  • document release or changeset expectations clearly
  • share cross-package tooling instead of repeating setup

docs.title: Project overview
docs.text: The react-modules repository provides a reusable package layer for frontend work in the MSF ecosystem. It follows a library-first structure so teams can consume shared components, hooks, or utilities without duplicating foundational code across application projects.

docs.title: Main responsibilities
docs.text:
This workspace is designed to cover:

  • shared frontend modules
  • package-level build and publishing conventions
  • workspace-level tooling and dependency coordination
  • publishable library primitives for downstream React apps

docs.title: Key conventions
docs.text:
"packageManager": "pnpm@10.29.2",
"workspaces": [
  "packages/*"
]

This structure keeps the library modular while preserving a single, consistent release path via changesets.

docs.title: Typical workflow
docs.text:
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test
pnpm release

docs.title: Development guidance
docs.text:
• keep modules reusable and generic
  • prefer stable interfaces for shared utilities
  • document package responsibilities clearly for consumers
  • validate packaging and release mechanics before making changes to public APIs
